reason: The 'who owns this service?' problem is real for me, but I'm not piping our Slack, GitHub and Drive into a startup's hosted preview, and I don't have the platform team hours to babysit yet another self-hosted Docker app. It goes on the 'look again next year' list next to the three other tools that promised the same thing.
objection: Handing read access to all our Slack and GitHub to a small company whose cloud is in early preview. Security review alone would take a quarter, and I'd still be the one explaining it if something leaked. Plus Glean and Confluence already half-cover this.
would_change_my_mind: A SOC 2 Type II report plus a peer engineering leader I trust telling me they self-hosted it and it actually cut ownership and incident questions, ideally with a read-only, single-repo pilot I can run in a week without security sign-off.
